articles.headline: Oil Holds Gain With Iran's Exports Strained as Conflict Drags On
articles.summary: West Texas Intermediate crude traded near $102 per barrel and Brent closed above $107 after a 4% gain the prior session, as the U.S.-Iran conflict continued and Iranian oil exports showed further strain. Satellite images confirmed no ocean-going tankers at Iran's Kharg Island export hub for several days — the first sign of an extended halt since the 10-week war began. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned the market is losing approximately 100 million barrels of supply per week, and said prolonged disruptions could delay market normalization until next year. President Trump was expected to press China's President Xi on Iran during their Beijing summit.

articles.headline: US to Release New Data on Global Oil Reserves, Hormuz Shipments Quarterly
articles.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration announced it will begin releasing new quarterly data on global strategic reserves and petroleum and LNG flows through key shipping choke points, beginning Wednesday. The new energy security datasets are designed to track how the war in Iran has upended global energy supply and altered key assumptions about oil markets. The report will provide indicators of how Strait of Hormuz disruptions are affecting global supply chains.

articles.headline: US Beef Prices Hit Record Highs as Trump Team Holds Off on Import Tariff Cuts
articles.summary: The Trump administration delayed a previously planned executive action to temporarily suspend beef import tariffs, despite earlier reports that the move was imminent. A White House official said the administration is still fine-tuning potential directives aimed at alleviating temporary domestic beef shortages. Beef prices have reached record highs as a result of supply constraints. The delay came after Trump was expected to sign the directives on Monday.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Inland Empire — Tireco, Medline, and Unis Among Q1 Deals
articles.summary: CoStar recognized the top Q1 2026 industrial leases in the Inland Empire, with prominent transactions signed by tire distributor Tireco, healthcare distributor Medline, and logistics operator Unis negotiated by CBRE. The Power Broker quarterly deals program evaluated all leases closed in Q1 and selected standout deals from CoStar's research team. Full deal terms are available to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Newmark Advises Anheuser-Busch on $360M Sale of Former Newark Facility to Goodman Group
articles.summary: Newmark Group advised Anheuser-Busch in the $360 million sale of its former brewing facility in Newark, New Jersey, to Goodman Group, a global industrial real estate owner and developer. The 75-year-old facility was closed by Anheuser-Busch in January 2026. Newmark Executive Vice Chairman Adam Doneger and Executive Managing Director Adam Petrillo served as exclusive advisors to the seller. Goodman Group plans to redevelop the site for industrial use.

articles.headline: Green Street Commercial Property Price Index Fell 0.1% in April; Life Science Properties Decline
articles.summary: Green Street's Commercial Property Price Index decreased 0.1% in April 2026, with life science property values declining and pricing in other sectors remaining essentially unchanged. The index, which measures REIT portfolio pricing on a frequently updated basis, has increased 2.3% over the past twelve months. Green Street Co-Head of Strategic Research Peter Rothemund had previously stated that roughly 2% annual price appreciation was his baseline expectation for 2026.

articles.headline: Green Street Expands News Platform to U.S. Subscribers for Real-Time CRE Intelligence
articles.summary: Green Street announced the expansion of its Green Street News digital platform to include U.S. subscribers, granting real-time access to first-to-market scoops across 25 global commercial real estate markets. The platform was previously available only to non-U.S. subscribers and delivers exclusive deal flow, capital markets intelligence, and sector news. The expansion makes Green Street's international CRE news coverage available to U.S. investors, lenders, and market leaders for the first time.

articles.headline: U.S. CPI Accelerates to 3.8% in April — Fastest Since 2023 — Driven by Energy and Services
articles.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released April 2026 CPI data showing headline inflation of 3.8% year-over-year — the fastest pace since 2023 — with a 0.6% month-over-month gain. Core CPI rose 0.4% for the month and 2.8% year-over-year, exceeding the 0.3% consensus estimate. Higher gasoline prices tied to Middle East conflict accounted for roughly one-third of the monthly headline increase. Services inflation rose 0.6% month-over-month, and food prices rose 0.5%, reflecting diesel-driven cost pass-through in the food distribution sector. The data fueled market bets on potential Federal Reserve rate hikes in 2027.

articles.headline: Fed Holds Rates at 3.5%–3.75% for Third Straight Meeting; Dissent Rises Over Inflation Risk
articles.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held the federal funds rate at 3.5%–3.75% at its April 29 meeting, the third consecutive hold, in an 8-4 vote — the most dissent since October 1992. The Fed acknowledged that Middle East developments have increased uncertainty around the economic outlook and flagged elevated upside risks to inflation. Fed Chair Jerome Powell's term expires May 15, with Kevin Warsh confirmed as his successor. Markets currently price in no changes to rates through year-end 2026, though interest-rate swaps now reflect a 70% probability of a rate hike by April 2027 following the hot April CPI print.

articles.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Aims for Stability on Trade; Breakthroughs Unlikely
articles.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing for his first visit since taking office, with trade and tariffs expected to dominate discussions with President Xi Jinping. Since Trump's last Beijing visit, U.S.-China merchandise trade has fallen by more than one-third. A one-year tariff truce between the two countries is in effect through November 10, 2026, including a reduction of fentanyl-related duties from 20% to 10%. Analysts described the summit as stability-focused with little expectation of major new breakthroughs on trade structure.

articles.headline: NorthPoint Development Starts Work on 428,900 SF Speculative Industrial Building in Chicago's 90 & Randall Logistics Park
articles.summary: NorthPoint Development commenced construction on a 428,900-square-foot speculative cross-dock warehouse at Interstate 90 and Randall Road in Algonquin, Illinois, within the 90 & Randall Logistics Park. The facility will feature a 40-foot clear height, 44 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 104 trailer stalls, and 277 car parking spaces. Peak Construction Corporation was awarded the general contracting contract, with studioNorth as architect and Atwell as civil engineer. The Kansas City, Missouri-based developer is building the property speculatively without a pre-signed tenant.

articles.headline: Weston Acquires 305,491 SF Class A Distribution Center in Huntsville, Alabama for $29.3M
articles.summary: Weston, a Cleveland, Ohio-based industrial real estate owner and operator, acquired River and Rocket Commerce Center — a 305,491-square-foot Class A industrial distribution facility at 23366 Bibb — in the Huntsville, Alabama area for $29.3 million. The acquisition reflects continued investor appetite for Class A logistics facilities in high-growth Sun Belt markets. Huntsville has been among the Southeast's most active industrial markets, driven by defense, aerospace, and advanced manufacturing demand.

articles.headline: Missner Group Buys 58,236 SF Multi-Tenant Industrial Building in Aurora, Illinois
articles.summary: The Missner Group acquired a 58,236-square-foot multi-tenant industrial building in Aurora, Illinois, with plans to lease up the property. The Chicago-area acquisition reflects continued investor interest in smaller multi-tenant industrial product in the greater Chicago logistics market. Aurora sits within the broader Chicago industrial corridor, which recorded strong absorption and a 6% vacancy rate as of early 2026. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

articles.headline: At China Summit, Trump Has CEOs, But Xi Has Leverage on Tariffs, Taiwan
articles.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, bringing an entourage of 16 A-list executives including Tesla's Elon Musk, Apple's Tim Cook, and Boeing's Kelly Ortberg. The two leaders are negotiating across trade, tech, Taiwan, and Iran-related issues, with each side pursuing different leverage strategies. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng held three hours of preparatory talks in Seoul on May 13. A trade truce reached last October is expected to be extended, with modest policy announcements anticipated.

articles.headline: US and China Wrap Up Trade Talks With Trump En Route to Beijing
articles.summary: Trade negotiators led by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China's Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded approximately three hours of talks in Seoul to prepare for the Trump-Xi summit. The Iran war and bilateral trade developments were among the top agenda items. The teams last met face-to-face in Paris two months ago, shortly after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran. No joint statement was issued following the preliminary meeting.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi to Weigh Tariff Cuts on $30 Billion of Imports in Managed Trade Push
articles.summary: The U.S. and China are expected to move toward a managed trade mechanism for non-sensitive goods at this week's summit, with each side potentially identifying approximately $30 billion worth of goods on which they could reduce tariffs. The proposed 'Board of Trade' mechanism was first raised by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in March as a key deliverable. China currently maintains a general 10% extra tariff on all U.S. imports, matching the current temporary 10% U.S. tariff on Chinese goods. Four people familiar with the Trump administration's objectives expected a $30 billion-for-$30 billion trade-barrier reduction framework.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh Wants to Change How You Think About Inflation — Potentially Terrible News for Wall Street
articles.summary: May 15 marks the final day of Jerome Powell's second term as Fed chair and the presumed beginning of Kevin Warsh's tenure. Warsh, a former FOMC voting member known for hawkish positions, wants to change the Fed's definition of inflation away from the formal 2% target. During his Senate Banking Committee testimony on April 21, Warsh said price stability should mean conditions where 'no one's talking about it.' The Iran war has fueled inflationary pressures that may make rate cuts unavailable under either chair.

articles.headline: Trump and Xi Dialed Down the Trade War, But Challenges Lurk at Their China Summit
articles.summary: China's share of goods imported to the U.S. has fallen from 22% at the start of Trump's first term in 2017 to just 7.5% in the first three months of 2026, according to U.S. Census Bureau data analyzed by the Peterson Institute for International Economics. A trade truce reached last October is likely to be extended at the Beijing summit, with China potentially announcing plans to buy American soybeans, beef, and Boeing aircraft. U.S. officials have proposed creating a Board of Trade to keep the sides engaged on economic issues. Despite Trump's claims about profiting from China trade, China bought nearly $50 billion less in American products last year than in 2022.

articles.headline: CoStar: Industrial Vacancy Remains in Mid-7% Range Entering Q2 2026, Expected to Edge Higher Into 2027
articles.summary: The national industrial vacancy rate remains in the mid-7% range entering the second quarter of 2026 and is expected to edge higher into 2027 before beginning a gradual descent, according to CoStar's latest revised forecast. West Coast port markets, particularly those exposed to Chinese trade, continue to underperform due to reduced demand, with availability in large, newer logistics properties near major West Coast ports exceeding 13%, compared to approximately 9% for East Coast port markets. Markets with elevated availability in new industrial construction such as Gainesville, Georgia, Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, and San Antonio, Texas face particular challenges. CoStar forecasts increasing industrial demand in the second half of 2026 that could accelerate lease-up of the supply overhang.

articles.headline: GlobeSt: Large Banks Ease Lending Standards While Construction Lending Weakens Amid Higher Costs
articles.summary: Large banks are easing credit standards for commercial real estate borrowers, according to the Fed's latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, while construction lending continues to weaken amid higher building material costs. The divergence reflects institutional CRE borrowers regaining access to capital for stabilized assets while development financing remains constrained. The trend aligns with a broader CRE market where top-performing assets can attract refinancing but speculative development faces continued headwinds.

articles.headline: CoStar: Industrial Vacancy at West Coast Port Markets Exceeds 13% as Chinese Trade Volume Falls
articles.summary: Availability in large, newer logistics properties near major West Coast ports exceeds 13%, compared to an average of approximately 9% for East Coast port markets, per CoStar data. China's share of U.S. imports fell to just 7.5% in early 2026, down from 22% at the start of Trump's first term in 2017, directly reducing demand at Southern California port-adjacent warehouse markets. The Birtcher Logistics Center, a 492,000-square-foot building in the Inland Empire that completed construction in early 2025, remains vacant, illustrating continued challenges in the supply overhang. CoStar projects that data centers will surpass warehouses in construction spending in 2026.

articles.headline: Goldman Sachs Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast as Inflation Lingers Near 3%
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs pushed its Fed rate-cut forecast back by one quarter, now expecting the next two cuts in December 2026 and March 2027, citing PCE inflation hovering near 3% — well above the Fed's 2% goal. The Fed held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% at its April 28-29 FOMC meeting amid four internal dissents, the most since 1992. Barclays dropped its September cut call entirely, now expecting no move until March 2027. JPMorgan Global Research expects the Fed to hold all year and sees the next move as a potential 25-basis-point hike.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh Confirmed as Federal Reserve Chair, Replacing Jerome Powell
articles.summary: Kevin Warsh was confirmed by the full Senate on May 13, replacing Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve Chair, whose term ends May 15. The transition arrives as April CPI came in at 3.8% year-over-year, well above the Fed's 2% target, creating an immediate challenge for the incoming chair. Markets no longer expect rate cuts in 2026, with BofA Global Research now projecting cuts may not come until mid or late 2027. Warsh would need to rally six other Fed governors to vote for any rate cut under current inflation conditions.

articles.headline: Data Centers Boost Otherwise Sagging Construction Pipeline
articles.summary: The Associated Builders and Contractors Construction Backlog Indicator rose to a 10-month high of 8.8 months in April, driven disproportionately by data center projects. The metric rose 0.2 months from March and 0.1 months from April 2025, with backlog surging for firms with more than $100M in annual revenue, a 2.2-month year-over-year jump. The data shows a stark split between large contractors benefiting from data center work and smaller firms that lack access to those projects. Just 1 in 5 respondents expected profit margins to decrease over the next six months, the lowest share since January 2025.

articles.headline: US Producer Prices Rise Most Since 2022 on Energy Costs
articles.summary: The U.S. Producer Price Index rose 6% year-over-year in April 2026, the largest annual increase since December 2022, topping all estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists. On a monthly basis, the PPI surged 1.4%, the largest gain since March 2022, driven primarily by a 15.6% surge in gasoline prices tied to the Iran war. Goods prices jumped 2% and services prices rose 1.2%, with truck transportation of freight and machinery and equipment wholesaling among the notable service-side increases. The April increase is nearly triple the 0.5% consensus forecast from economists.

articles.headline: Bond Investors Flee as Inflation Worry Sends Yields to 2026 High
articles.summary: Following back-to-back hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation reports this week, investors fled government bonds, sending benchmark 10-year Treasury yields to their highest level since July 2025. The 30-year Treasury yield briefly traded above 5% as the latest PPI data pushed traders to increase bets on a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in the coming year. The Fed currently holds its benchmark rate at 3.50%–3.75% following an 8-4 vote at its April 29 meeting. Market pricing now shows roughly a 39% chance of a rate hike by year-end, up sharply from prior weeks.

articles.headline: Why US Inflation Matters for British Investors
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Money Distilled newsletter published May 13, 2026, examined the threat of rising U.S. interest rates following April's hot CPI reading of 3.8% and the even hotter PPI report released Wednesday. The newsletter referenced Federal Reserve Chair nominee Kevin Warsh and the potential knock-on effects for global assets from elevated U.S. inflation. The April CPI came in at 3.8% annually — the fastest pace since 2023 — with energy prices accounting for roughly one-third of the monthly increase, tied to the Iran war's impact on the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Walmart Cuts or Relocates About 1,000 Corporate Workers in Tech Consolidation
articles.summary: Walmart announced it would cut or relocate approximately 1,000 corporate employees in its technology and product divisions as the retail giant completes a shift to a unified global technology platform, the Wall Street Journal first reported. The restructuring was directed by Global CTO Suresh Kumar and EVP of AI Acceleration Daniel Danker, who cited the consolidation of previously siloed tech teams working on duplicate problems across Walmart U.S., Sam's Club, and international units. Affected workers are being offered internal positions or relocation to Walmart's Bentonville, Arkansas headquarters or its Northern California offices. The round brings total 2026 corporate roles affected to roughly 1,100, following an earlier 1,500-position reduction in May 2025.

articles.headline: Wall Street Gets More Anxious About Long-Term Inflation
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the gap between yields on ordinary U.S. Treasurys and Treasury inflation-protected securities — known as the break-even rate — recently hit its highest level since October 2022, according to Federal Reserve data. The elevated break-even rate signals that investors expect average annual inflation of approximately 2.7% over the next five years. The reading follows April's CPI print of 3.8% and Wednesday's PPI report showing a 6% annual increase, both well above the Fed's 2% target. Wall Street has scaled back any near-term expectations for Fed rate cuts following the dual inflation reports.

articles.headline: Investors Back Blackstone's Industrial Bet With $4 Billion in New Refinancings
articles.summary: Blackstone is completing its third major industrial portfolio refinancing of 2026 through its Link Logistics affiliate, locking in a total of more than $4 billion in new floating-rate CMBS debt across 213 warehouse and logistics properties. The latest deal, BX Trust 2026-CIP, is a $1.3 billion mortgage loan secured by 83 industrial properties spanning 13 million square feet across 15 states, scheduled to close May 21 with co-origination from Deutsche Bank, Citi, JPMorgan, Nomura, and Goldman Sachs. The three 2026 refinancings combined cover 30.9 million square feet and drew participation from at least 12 major lending institutions. Fitch noted that in-place rents of $7.75 per square foot across the latest portfolio trail average market rents of $10.50 per square foot, providing a built-in rent growth narrative for lenders.

articles.headline: CoStar: U.S. Industrial Vacancy Projected to Rise Into Early 2027
articles.summary: According to the most recent CoStar forecast, the national industrial vacancy rate remains in the mid-7% range entering Q2 2026 and is projected to edge higher into early 2027 before beginning a gradual descent, a slightly worse outlook than prior expectations. CoStar cited a near-term energy price spike that has eroded consumer spending power, along with downgraded employment growth forecasts tied to tariff policy changes and slower labor force growth. The revised forecast noted that risks are tilted to the downside, with elevated tariffs or weaker consumer goods spending potentially pushing vacancy to 8–9%. Rent growth is projected at approximately 2.2% annually over 2026–27, below the pre-pandemic five-year average.

articles.headline: Tech Carries Wall Street to Records Even as Most Stocks Fall After Discouraging Inflation Data
articles.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to a new record close of 7,444.25 on Wednesday and the Nasdaq added 1.2% to 26,402.34, both hitting fresh intraday and closing records, driven by technology sector outperformance. However, roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 components fell during the session as the hotter-than-expected April PPI report of 6% year-over-year weighed on retail, banking, and other cyclically sensitive sectors. Nvidia shares closed up more than 2% and Micron Technology gained more than 4%, as investors anticipated positive semiconductor developments from Trump's Beijing summit with Xi Jinping. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 67.36 points, or 0.14%, ending at 49,693.20.

articles.headline: Wholesale Prices Surge 1.4% in April — Largest Monthly Gain Since March 2022
articles.summary: The April 2026 Producer Price Index released Wednesday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed wholesale prices rose 1.4% month-over-month, the largest monthly increase since March 2022, and 6.0% year-over-year, the largest annual gain since December 2022. Goods prices surged 2%, led by a 15.6% jump in gasoline, while services prices rose 1.2%, with a 3.5% increase in margins for machinery and equipment wholesaling and higher truck transportation of freight costs. Core PPI excluding food and energy accelerated 1%, compared to the 0.4% estimate. Nationwide senior economist Ben Ayers said the jump in input prices portends further consumer price increases in May, forecasting CPI above 4% in next month's report.

articles.headline: Stonelake Capital Partners Acquires Apex Commerce Center Industrial Portfolio in Raleigh for $90M
articles.summary: Stonelake Capital Partners acquired Apex Commerce Center, a three-building Class A industrial portfolio totaling 613,353 square feet in Raleigh, North Carolina, for $90 million, closing immediately after construction completion in April 2026. The three buildings are located at 2061 Production Drive, 2170 Production Drive, and 600 Pristine Water Drive in the Apex submarket. No seller or tenant details were disclosed in the Connect CRE report. The transaction reflects continued investor demand for newly built Class A industrial product in Southeastern U.S. logistics markets.

articles.headline: BGO and Greenlaw Partners Purchase River Park 6 Warehouse in Atlanta Submarket for $70M
articles.summary: BentallGreenOak (BGO) and Greenlaw Partners purchased River Park 6, a 724,687-square-foot warehouse in Butts County, Georgia, for $70 million from sellers Waterloo Partners and ICM Property Group. The building is part of the River Park industrial campus, which is planned to ultimately reach 21 million square feet. Luggage brand Travelpro leases a portion of River Park 6. The deal adds to BGO's growing industrial portfolio in the Southeast as the Atlanta market continues to absorb excess post-pandemic supply.

articles.headline: Phoenix Developers Converting Office Complexes Into Industrial Parks
articles.summary: Lincoln Property and Panattoni Development have both recently announced plans to either demolish or reposition office buildings in the Phoenix metro area in favor of industrial uses. Lincoln Property's Sky Harbor Innovation Park sits on approximately 19 acres at 1920 W. University Drive, just west of Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. The trend of office-to-industrial conversion has accelerated in Phoenix as vacancy in suburban office parks rises and demand for infill industrial and flex space in urban-adjacent locations remains active. No financial terms were disclosed for either project.

articles.headline: FedEx Ground Distribution Facility Sold in Kentucky After 17-Year Hold
articles.summary: SURMOUNT, a net lease real estate advisory and investment platform, arranged the sale of an 82,754-square-foot FedEx Ground distribution facility at 2500 Eich Road in Paducah, Kentucky. SURMOUNT's Rocco Driscoll and Anthony Bird represented the seller, a private investor, following a nearly 17-year hold period. No buyer identity or sale price was disclosed. The transaction underscores continued investor appetite for net-leased logistics assets occupied by national carriers.

articles.headline: Prologis Names Chief Development Officer as Firm Plans $8 Billion Data Center Push
articles.summary: Industrial real estate giant Prologis tapped veteran executive Damon Austin to join its C-suite as Chief Development Officer as the company plans to spend $8 billion over the next four years on data center development. Austin's appointment signals Prologis's strategic pivot toward data center infrastructure alongside its core logistics portfolio, capitalizing on surging demand from artificial intelligence-driven hyperscaler tenants. The data center investment represents a significant expansion of Prologis's development scope beyond traditional warehouse and distribution facilities. No specific projects or locations were disclosed in the announcement.

articles.headline: IEA Oil Market Report — May 2026: Record Supply Losses as Hormuz Disruption Deepens
articles.summary: The International Energy Agency's May 2026 Oil Market Report warns that more than ten weeks after the Iran war began, Strait of Hormuz supply losses are depleting global oil inventories at a record pace. Cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceed 1 billion barrels, with more than 14 million barrels per day shut in — described by the IEA as the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market. Global oil supply declined a further 1.8 mb/d in April to 95.1 mb/d, with WTI crude trading around $102-$110 per barrel. The IEA assumes Hormuz flows could gradually resume from Q3 2026, but warns of further price volatility ahead of the peak summer demand period.

articles.headline: US and China Seek to Repair Damage from Tariff War That Sent Trade Into a Freefall
articles.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing on May 13, 2026, for a summit with President Xi Jinping aimed at stabilizing the U.S.-China trade relationship after a tumultuous year. U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods currently stand at approximately 48%, even after coming down from triple-digit levels briefly hit in 2025; China's share of U.S. trade has fallen from over 13% in 2016 to 6.4% last year. Many American companies have shifted production to Vietnam and India, while Chinese manufacturers have scrambled to find customers in Europe and Southeast Asia. Factory owners in China expressed hopes for at least incremental improvement, though prospects for a return to pre-tariff trade volumes are considered slim.

articles.headline: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Rise to New Records as Tech Leads Despite Hot Wholesale Inflation Print
articles.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,444.25 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.20% to 26,402.34, both reaching new all-time intraday and closing records on May 13, 2026, despite a hotter-than-expected April PPI report. WTI crude finished the day at approximately $102 per barrel, with high oil prices driven by continued Strait of Hormuz disruption contributing to elevated inflation. After the close, Cisco Systems surged 18% after posting Q3 results and guidance that beat expectations while announcing nearly 4,000 job cuts. April retail sales data and initial jobless claims are scheduled for release Thursday.

articles.headline: Wholesale Inflation Shoots to +6.0% Year-Over-Year in April 2026: PPI Report Details
articles.summary: April's Producer Price Index rose a seasonally adjusted 1.4% month-over-month and 6% year-over-year — the largest annual gain since December 2022 — against a consensus forecast of just 0.5% for the month. Energy was the primary driver, with gasoline prices surging 15.6% on a monthly basis due to the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz closure. Services inflation accelerated 1.2%, the biggest monthly gain since March 2022, led by a 2.7% rise in trade services and a 3.5% jump in machinery and equipment wholesaling margins; truck transportation of freight costs also increased. The Fed has kept its benchmark rate in the 3.5%-3.75% range, with market pricing now showing about 39% odds of a rate hike in the next 12 months.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh Confirmed as Federal Reserve Chair, Succeeding Jerome Powell
articles.summary: The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve Chair in a 54-45 vote on Wednesday, May 13, the most partisan confirmation vote in the Fed's modern era. Warsh, 56, succeeds Jerome Powell whose four-year term as chair expires Friday, May 15, though Powell will remain on the Fed's Board of Governors through 2028. Warsh takes office as April CPI hit 3.8% year-over-year — a near three-year high — and markets are pricing in a 97% chance the Fed holds rates unchanged at the June 16-17 FOMC meeting, his first as chair. Trump has publicly pressed for rate cuts, while inflation driven by the U.S.-Iran war's energy shock complicates any near-term easing.

articles.headline: April Producer Price Index Surges 1.4% Month-Over-Month, Biggest Jump Since March 2022
articles.summary: U.S. producer prices rose 1.4% month-over-month in April 2026, the largest monthly increase since March 2022, far exceeding the 0.5% consensus forecast. Goods prices jumped 2.0%, led by a 15.6% surge in gasoline costs driven by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict disrupting Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic. Year-over-year, producer prices jumped 6.0%, the biggest annual increase since December 2022. Services prices also rose 1.2%, with truck transportation of freight and machinery and equipment wholesaling among the key contributors, signaling rising pipeline inflation for business costs.

articles.headline: April CPI Rises 3.8% Year-Over-Year, Energy and Shelter Drive Monthly Gain
articles.summary: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers increased 0.6% on a seasonally adjusted basis in April 2026, following a 0.9% rise in March, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Over the last 12 months, the all-items index rose 3.8%, the highest rate in nearly three years. Energy prices rose 3.8% in April, accounting for over 40% of the monthly increase, while shelter rose 0.6% and food at home rose 0.7%. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, rose 0.4% for the month and 2.8% year-over-year. The hotter-than-expected print sent Treasury yields sharply higher and wiped out most market expectations for a 2026 rate cut.

articles.headline: April Retail Sales Data Released; Census Bureau Report Scheduled for May 14
articles.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau released the April 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Sales report on May 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. EDT. Ahead of the official data, the CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor showed total retail sales excluding autos and gasoline rose 0.34% month-over-month and 5.73% year-over-year in April. NRF President and CEO Matthew Shay stated that consumers continued spending despite higher gas prices from the Iran conflict, cautious sentiment, and persistent inflation concerns. Sales growth was led by clothing, sporting goods, and health and personal care stores. March retail sales had come in at $752.1 billion, up 1.7% from the prior month and 4.0% year-over-year.

articles.headline: CoStar World News for May 14: Blackstone French Industrial Deal, Data Center Capital Crunch
articles.summary: CoStar's daily global news roundup for May 14, 2026 highlighted Blackstone's previously announced €2.3 billion acquisition of Proudreed's French industrial portfolio of more than 500 sites and 2.2 million square meters, with Blackstone planning to accelerate development to reach 115,000–120,000 square meters of new properties annually. The roundup also flagged a growing capital crunch in data center development, with industry estimates pegging total capital needs at as much as $1 trillion over the next five years as construction costs for AI and cloud facilities surge. Additional items covered UK commercial real estate new lending rising 29% in 2025 to a decade high, and German real estate prices increasing 2.2% annually in Q1 2026.

articles.headline: New Rexford CEO Laura Clark Focused on 'Operational Rigor' at Southern California Industrial REIT
articles.summary: CoStar published a profile of Laura Clark, the new CEO of Rexford Industrial Realty, who took the helm of one of Southern California's largest industrial landlords after building a career spanning multiple property types including retail, hotels, student housing, and industrial. Clark indicated her strategic focus will center less on building large amounts of new space and more on owning strategically located warehouses that are increasingly difficult to replicate. Clark's background includes time at Green Street Advisors in financial analysis before rising through industrial real estate. Rexford Industrial focuses exclusively on infill Southern California industrial markets including the Inland Empire, Los Angeles, and Orange County.

articles.headline: BGO and Greenlaw Partners Acquire River Park 6 Industrial Warehouse in Georgia for $70M
articles.summary: BentallGreenOak (BGO) and Greenlaw Partners purchased River Park 6, a 724,687-square-foot warehouse in Butts County, Georgia, for $70 million from sellers Waterloo Partners and ICM Property Group. The facility is part of the River Park industrial campus, which is slated to grow to 21 million square feet of space. Travelpro currently leases part of River Park 6. The acquisition expands BGO and Greenlaw's industrial footprint in the Southeast Atlanta logistics corridor.

articles.headline: Large Banks Ease CRE Lending Standards While Construction Lending Weakens Amid Higher Costs
articles.summary: GlobeSt reported that large banks have begun easing lending standards for commercial real estate borrowers, according to recent survey data, while construction lending has simultaneously weakened amid persistently higher construction costs. The divergence reflects improving liquidity conditions for stabilized assets but ongoing hesitancy to finance new development. The trend is consistent with CoStar data showing the national industrial vacancy rate remaining in the mid-7% range entering Q2 2026, with vacancy projected to edge higher into 2027 before beginning a gradual descent.

articles.headline: Trump-Xi Summit on May 14–15 to Tackle AI Guardrails Between World's Two Largest Economies
articles.summary: A Trump-Xi summit is scheduled for May 14–15, 2026, with AI governance and guardrails between the U.S. and China as a key agenda item, according to market coverage from multiple outlets including Bloomberg. The summit follows the November 2025 one-year tariff truce extension, which reduced bilateral tariffs on each other's goods and included reductions in U.S. fentanyl-related tariffs on China from 20% to 10% through November 10, 2026. Semiconductor and technology company stocks are expected to react sharply to any outcome. U.S. universal tariffs officially remain at 10% until July 24, with threats they could rise to 15% if no broader deal is reached.

articles.headline: Apartment Construction Starts Plummet to 15-Year Low
articles.summary: BisNow reported that apartment construction starts have fallen to a 15-year low nationally, according to new data released in mid-May 2026. The sharp decline reflects a combination of high borrowing costs, elevated construction costs, and reduced investor appetite for new multifamily development. The dropoff in residential construction is occurring simultaneously with reduced industrial development starts, which PwC/ULI research has pegged at down 25% versus the 2017–2019 average through 2025 year-to-date. The broader contraction in construction starts affects demand for building materials supply chains and construction-related industrial tenants.

articles.headline: Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin Mulls City Near Austin to House Next Big Venture
articles.summary: BisNow reported that Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin is considering developing a company-sponsored city near Austin, Texas, to house its next major venture, according to sources familiar with the plans. No specific location or timeline was confirmed. The report adds to a broader trend of major technology and aerospace companies seeking to develop large-scale campus or community infrastructure to support their operations and workforce. Blue Origin is a major aerospace manufacturer and launch services provider with growing logistics and infrastructure footprints.

articles.headline: US Retail Sales Rise for Third Month Despite Gas Price Surge
articles.summary: U.S. retail sales advanced for a third consecutive month in April, gaining 0.5% from March and rising 4.9% year-over-year, according to the Census Bureau. The increase occurred despite a 3.8% annualized rise in the Consumer Price Index and diminished consumer confidence amid war-driven energy cost surges. Nine of 13 retail categories posted gains, while furniture stores (-2%), department stores (-3.2%), car dealerships (-0.5%), and clothing shops (-1.5%) all declined. Unemployment held steady at 4.3% with employers adding 115,000 jobs in April, supporting continued consumer spending.

articles.headline: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Tops 7,500 as AI Trade Fuels Record-Breaking Run
articles.summary: The S&P 500 surpassed 7,500 on May 14, driven by a revival of the artificial intelligence trade and strong April retail sales data showing consumer resilience despite war-driven energy cost surges. Nvidia climbed for a seventh straight day and Cisco Systems rose 13% after a solid earnings outlook. AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems surged 89% in its Nasdaq trading debut after raising $5.55 billion in the year's largest IPO, priced at $185 per share. Ford Motor Co. also extended gains on enthusiasm around firms positioned to benefit from power-hungry data centers.

articles.headline: AI Chipmaker Cerebras Shares Soar 89% After Year's Biggest IPO
articles.summary: AI chipmaker and data center firm Cerebras Systems raised $5.55 billion in its Nasdaq IPO, priced at $185 per share — above the marketed range — giving it an initial market value of approximately $40 billion. Shares opened at $350, up 89%, pushing the valuation above $100 billion on a fully diluted basis. Demand for the offering exceeded available shares by more than 20 times. The company has partnerships with Amazon Web Services and OpenAI, and the debut is viewed as an early test of investor appetite ahead of potential larger offerings from SpaceX and OpenAI later in 2026.

articles.headline: Foundry Commercial Nabs North Texas Office Complex to Build Industrial Facility
articles.summary: Foundry Commercial, a real estate firm pioneering office-to-industrial conversions across the United States, is adding to its pipeline in the Dallas-Fort Worth region with the acquisition of a North Texas office complex intended for industrial redevelopment. The company is executing a broader strategy to demolish and replace approximately 1.9 million square feet of existing office properties with 2.9 million square feet of new industrial space across multiple U.S. markets. Foundry has previously executed similar conversions in Jacksonville, Florida, and other Sun Belt markets. The article is exclusively available to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Proprietary Data Obsession Is Holding Real Estate Back From AI
articles.summary: At Bisnow's New York AI & Technology event held at Silverstein Properties' 7 World Trade Center on May 13, industry executives discussed how real estate firms' reluctance to share proprietary data with AI platforms is limiting adoption of the technology. Fundrise CEO Ben Miller stated that real estate companies are 'afraid to adopt the cutting-edge' AI tools due to concerns about data exposure to large language models. Onyxia Cyber CEO Sivan Tehila warned of 'shadow AI,' where employees use AI tools without authorization, potentially leaking sensitive company data. IBM research cited at the event found that over one-third of employees admit sharing sensitive work information with AI tools without employer permission.

articles.headline: Market Outlook: U.S. Retail Sales Resilience Adds to Inflation Pressure
articles.summary: Strong U.S. retail sales in April are reinforcing concerns that inflation pressures could remain elevated as consumers continue spending despite rising costs linked to the Iran war. Rising inflation expectations tied to energy prices are increasing pressure on bond markets and pushing Treasury yields higher, with markets still expecting central banks to hold interest rates steady through 2026. BMO Global Asset Management's Earl Davis noted that while consumer growth supports corporate bonds, investors should favor shorter-duration corporate paper — two-to-five year bonds — rather than 10-year Treasuries given inflation risk. The resilience of consumer demand despite record-low consumer sentiment signals sustained distribution and logistics activity.

articles.headline: Treasury Yields Little Changed as April Import and Export Prices Soar Above Wall Street Expectations
articles.summary: April import prices jumped 1.9% month-over-month — a full percentage point above March's move and well above the 0.9% consensus — pushing the 12-month rate to 4.2%, the most since October 2022. Fuels and lubricants surged 16.3% while petroleum products rose 19%, driven by the Iran war's impact on energy supply. The producer price index rose 1.4% in April, the biggest monthly increase since March 2022, with the annual rate reaching 6%. Core CPI came in at 2.8% annually, keeping the Fed on hold as newly confirmed Chair Kevin Warsh faces mounting inflation pressure from both the Iran conflict and tariffs.

articles.headline: Webinar: Distress Cycle Evolves as $520B of Maturities Looms
articles.summary: With roughly $52 billion of maturing commercial real estate debt considered at-risk out of $520 billion coming due in 2026, industry leaders reported that CRE distress is expanding beyond the office sector. Andrew Hundertmark, Vice Chairman at Argentic Services, told the Connect CRE webinar that office distress has decreased while more multifamily and hospitality distress is arriving. LNR Partners' Randall Rosen said major metro office markets — with Chicago cited specifically — continue to struggle significantly. The panel discussed evolving strategies for lenders and special servicers navigating the active distress environment.

articles.headline: Return to Lender: Week of May 14, 2026
articles.summary: Connect CRE's weekly CMBS distress tracker reports multiple loans entering special servicing, including the $64.5 million Summit Place Wisconsin loan (CD 2016-CD3 & JPMDB 2017-C5) after the borrower indicated it would no longer fund operating shortfalls. A prominent Houston Galleria-area office tower at 3000 Post Oak Blvd faces foreclosure after its $80 million loan matured vacant. The Decoration & Design Building in New York moved to special servicing upon hitting its May 2026 maturity date on a CGCMT-securitized loan. The Seattle Bravern office complex — formerly leased to Microsoft — had a court-approved sale overseen by Eastdil Secured following a $304 million mortgage default.

articles.headline: California People and Company News, Week of May 15, 2026
articles.summary: Transwestern Development hired Clark Neuhoff as Regional Partner for its West Coast Industrial Team, based in Newport Beach, CA, where he will source and execute institutional industrial development projects across the West Coast. Neuhoff previously served as CIO at Alere Property Group and was placed through executive search firm RETS Associates. Continental Development Corporation (CDC), one of the largest South Bay real estate developers with over 2 million square feet along the Rosecrans Corridor and 500,000 square feet of medical office in Torrance, appointed Robert Peddicord as EVP overseeing property management and leasing. Marcus & Millichap named Michael Puline as senior managing director and national director of its retail division; Puline previously led national retailer strategy for a $9 billion, 19-million-square-foot retail portfolio at a Blackstone portfolio company.

articles.headline: Texas Might Soon Have More Data Centers, But Investors Still Prefer Northern Virginia
articles.summary: JLL projected this year that Texas will surpass Virginia as the leading state for data center development by 2030 as AI mega-projects gravitate toward markets with more land and power capacity. Northern Virginia maintained a 0.5% data center vacancy rate at end-2025 after absorbing more than 1 gigawatt of capacity in 2025, and retains the highest rental rates of any data center market nationally, per CBRE. Speakers at Bisnow's national Data Center Investment Conference and Expo noted that Ashburn cannot compete with West Texas on megawatts but will maintain higher unit rents and lower vacancy, making it a superior investment on a per-unit basis. The Manhattan-sized AI campuses driving the current boom require power capacity and land that Northern Virginia fundamentally cannot provide.

articles.headline: Who Has the Power? Industrial and Data Centers Battle for Gigawatts
articles.summary: Data center construction and the AI boom are creating a structural competition with industrial/logistics users for electrical grid capacity, with data centers projected to reach 12% of national electricity demand by 2028, up from just over 4% in 2023. CBRE research shows tech and data center occupiers accounted for the largest share of manufacturing leasing in Q1 2026, driving a significant jump in manufacturing leasing from the prior year. Companies supporting the data center supply chain — including prefabrication contractors, component manufacturers, and maintenance operators — are leasing industrial space at growing rates, which Prologis described as a new structural driver within logistics real estate demand. Columbus, Ohio recorded 13 million square feet of net industrial absorption in 2025, trailing only Dallas and Phoenix, driven by data center growth and a major chip fabrication project.

articles.headline: Greer: US, China Willing to Continue Trade Truce
articles.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, speaking exclusively to Bloomberg on the sidelines of the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, signaled cautious optimism that US-China trade relations are stabilizing. Greer cited progress on agriculture purchases and rare earth supplies, though tariffs and supply chain issues remain unresolved. He stated the U.S. expects China to commit to 'double-digit billion' agricultural purchases per year over the next three years. The two presidents are anticipated to extend the one-year trade war pause agreed to in South Korea in October 2025.

articles.headline: US Expects Dramatic Agricultural Purchases by China, Greer Says
articles.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Bloomberg Television that the U.S. anticipates China will commit to billions in American agricultural purchases as the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing concludes. Greer specifically referenced 'double-digit billion' annual aggregate agricultural purchases — not just soybeans — over a three-year period. The average U.S. tariff on Chinese goods currently stands at 47.5% following the South Korea summit, up from 3.1% before Trump's first term, per the Peterson Institute for International Economics. Two-way goods trade between the U.S. and China totaled approximately $415 billion in 2025, down sharply from a $690 billion peak in 2022.

articles.headline: Kevin Warsh Confirmed New Fed Chair as Inflation Kicks Higher, Complicating the Central Bank's Path
articles.summary: Kevin Warsh was confirmed by the U.S. Senate in a 54-45 vote — the most divisive in Fed history — to replace Jerome Powell, whose chair term expires May 15, 2026. The Consumer Price Index rose 3.8% year-over-year in April, up from 3.3% in March, with energy prices accounting for 40% of the increase. Wholesale PPI surged 6.0% annually versus expectations of 4.9%, raising the prospect of rate hikes rather than cuts. The Federal Reserve has held its benchmark Federal Funds Rate steady at 3.50%–3.75% for its past three meetings, and J.P. Morgan strategists' base case is now for rates to remain steady through the end of 2026.

articles.headline: New York People and Company News, Week of May 15, 2026
articles.summary: Latham & Watkins LLP announced that Marco Caffuzzi has joined its New York office as a partner in the Real Estate Practice, bringing extensive experience in real estate financings, restructurings, joint ventures, and large-scale development transactions; he joins from Skadden, Arps. Avison Young made five strategic hires in New York City, including Christian Stanton and Libby Hodes focused on retail, two executive directors for office tenant representation, and a director on the Tri-State Investment Sales team. CRH, a leading building materials provider, appointed Aylwyn Bryan as CFO.

articles.headline: From Bad to Worse: The Federal Reserve's May Inflation Forecast Is Terrible News for Stock Investors
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland updated its May inflation nowcast to 4.2% CPI year-over-year, which would be the highest reading since April 2023. April CPI already came in at 3.8%, driven by gas prices averaging $4.50 per gallon nationally — up roughly 50% since the US-Iran conflict began February 28 and closed the Strait of Hormuz to commercial vessels. A Cleveland Fed CEO survey found manufacturing and services sector leaders expect inflation to average 3.7% over the next 12 months, up from 3.1% in the prior survey. Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh inherits the rate-setting challenge with his first FOMC decision set for June 16-17.

articles.headline: Blackstone's Data Center REIT Raises $1.75 Billion in IPO to Buy Data Centers
articles.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) completed its US IPO on May 14 on the NYSE, pricing 87.5 million shares at $20 each to raise $1.75 billion, with underwriters holding a 30-day option to lift total proceeds to $2 billion. The REIT will focus on acquiring newly constructed, stabilized data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion, occupied by investment-grade hyperscale tenants on long-term leases, targeting yields of 5.75% to 7%. Blackstone has identified approximately $25 billion in potential near-term data center purchases in Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin. Nick Pell, former president and CIO of Blackstone's Link Logistics industrial REIT arm, was appointed CEO of the new entity.

articles.headline: Texas People & Companies, May 15, 2026
articles.summary: Stream Realty Partners broke ground on Northfield Logistics Center, a Class A industrial development at 4330 Northfield Lane in Houston's infill Northwest submarket. The project will deliver more than 300,000 square feet of Class A distribution space. Rosenberger Construction is serving as the general contractor and Seeberger Architecture is the project architect. No tenant has been announced for the project.

articles.headline: CBRE Arranges $30.9 Million Sale of Treasure Coast Commerce Center Portfolio in Stuart, Florida
articles.summary: CBRE arranged the $30.9 million sale of the Treasure Coast Commerce Center Portfolio, a seven-building, multitenant industrial portfolio totaling 153,198 square feet in Stuart, Florida. CBRE represented both the seller, Ted Glasrud Associates, Inc., and the buyer, NorthBridge Partners, in the transaction. No lease terms or vacancy details for the portfolio were disclosed. The deal reflects continued investor demand for multitenant industrial product in secondary Florida markets.

articles.headline: US Industrial Production Rises by Most in Over a Year
articles.summary: U.S. industrial production posted its largest gain in over a year, according to Federal Reserve data released May 15. The report covers output at factories, mines, and utilities, following a March decline of 0.5% attributed to the Iran war's impact on factory and utility output. The data was featured as a top headline on Bloomberg's homepage on May 15, 2026, alongside reporting on the Xi-Trump summit framework.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Pressure Bonds: Back-to-Back Inflation Reports and Heightened Energy Prices Drive Yields to Highest in Nearly a Year
articles.summary: Back-to-back U.S. inflation reports combined with heightened energy prices from the Strait of Hormuz closure and mounting political uncertainty drove investors out of global bond markets on May 15, pushing benchmark interest rates to their highest levels in nearly a year. The 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest since July and 30-year yields traded above 5% following accelerating wholesale price data. Consumer prices rose 3.8% year-over-year in April, the hottest inflation reading since May 2023.

articles.headline: Stocks Fall as Inflation Jitters Lift Bond Yields: Markets Wrap
articles.summary: A global bond selloff halted a recent stock rally on May 15, with concerns intensifying that central banks will be forced to tighten policy further. Sector data showed Materials down 2.53%, Consumer Discretionary down 1.81%, and Industrials down 1.73% as of midday trading. The day prior, the S&P 500 had surged past 7,500 for the first time and the Dow crossed 50,000, driven by AI stock gains and optimism from the Trump-Xi summit.

articles.headline: Oil Headed for Weekly Gain as Strait of Hormuz Remains Effectively Closed
articles.summary: Oil prices were on track for a weekly gain as the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed amid the ongoing Iran war, with efforts to end the conflict still in limbo. The closure has upended global energy markets, with both Trump and Xi agreeing at their Beijing summit that the Strait must remain open to support the free flow of energy. The sustained disruption has contributed to elevated energy prices that are feeding into already-sticky inflation.

articles.headline: Blackstone's Data Center REIT Hits Its $1.75B Initial Target In Debut
articles.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust raised $1.75 billion in its NYSE debut on May 14, selling 87.5 million shares at $20 per share, with underwriters holding a 30-day option to lift total proceeds to $2 billion. The REIT is a 'blind pool' with no assets yet identified, targeting acquisition of newly built data centers occupied by hyperscalers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion. Blackstone has identified approximately $25 billion in potential near-term data center purchases in Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin.

articles.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Concludes: China Agrees to Buy U.S. Oil and 200 Boeing Aircraft; 'Strategic Stability' Framework Set for Three Years
articles.summary: President Trump concluded his two-day Beijing summit with President Xi Jinping on May 15, with Trump announcing China agreed to purchase U.S. oil and 200 Boeing aircraft. Xi and Trump agreed to a 'strategic stability' framework to govern the bilateral relationship for the next three years, though no major formal trade agreements were announced before Trump departed. The two leaders agreed that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open for global energy flows and invited Xi for a White House visit on September 24; the one-year trade truce set in October 2025 remains in place, with average U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 47.5%.

articles.headline: Westmount Hires Industrial Veteran; SRS Expands National Retail Team; CenterSquare Adds AI Director
articles.summary: Westmount Realty Capital appointed Mike Demperio as director of development in Atlanta, bringing over five decades of industrial real estate experience and more than 100 million square feet of industrial projects across the country valued at over $4 billion. Demperio previously served as EVP at CRG and held roles at CBRE where he launched the firm's Global Logistics practice. SRS Real Estate Partners added Neill Kelly and Benjamin Gould to its national retail team to bolster restructuring and dispositions capability. CenterSquare Investment Management also appointed Doug Carpenter as its new director and head of data strategy and artificial intelligence.

articles.headline: Small Bay Now Dominates Industrial and It Will Stay That Way
articles.summary: GlobeSt published an analysis on May 14, 2026 examining how small-bay industrial product has become the dominant force in the industrial market. HALO businesses and the evolution of the broader economy were cited as major demand drivers behind the shift. Small-bay and micro-warehouse assets in last-mile and infill locations continue to post vacancy rates below 5%, making them among the most competitive subsectors in the market. The analysis concludes that the structural demand for small-bay industrial is durable and unlikely to reverse.

articles.headline: Betting on Continued Industrial Demand, Redfearn Capital Closes Pair of Deals Across Florida Totaling $60M
articles.summary: Redfearn Capital closed two industrial deals in South Florida and Jacksonville totaling $60 million, in what the firm described as a vote of confidence in Florida's industrial market. The transactions represent the new group's entry into the Florida industrial investment space. No specific property addresses or tenant details were disclosed in publicly available information. The deals signal continued private capital appetite for industrial assets in the Southeast despite broader market uncertainty.

articles.headline: Inflation and Fed Policy Are on Collision Course, Page Says
articles.summary: T. Rowe Price CIO Sébastien Page stated on Bloomberg Surveillance that the primary risk in financial markets is a 'collision course between inflation and Fed policy.' This comes as Jerome Powell's term as Fed Chair ended May 15, with the U.S. Senate confirming Kevin Warsh as his successor. Warsh is viewed as more open to rate cuts, but persistent inflation data has made near-term Fed rate cuts unlikely.

articles.headline: Inflation Rate Projected to Hit 6% in the Second Quarter, Top Economic Forecasters Say
articles.summary: The Survey of Professional Forecasters — a blue-ribbon group polled each quarter by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia — projected consumer price inflation to hit 6% in Q2 2026. The projection comes amid an ongoing energy price shock tied to geopolitical conflict and persistent supply disruptions. The forecast reinforces growing concerns that inflationary pressures are becoming more entrenched, complicating the Federal Reserve's efforts to guide inflation back to its 2% target.

articles.headline: U.S. Retail Sales Rise in April Despite Inflation and Higher Energy Costs
articles.summary: The U.S. Census Bureau's Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey for April 2026 showed retail and food services sales of $757.1 billion, up 0.5% from March and up 4.9% from April 2025. Retail trade sales were up 5.2% year-over-year, and nonstore retailers—the e-commerce proxy—rose 11.1% from a year ago. Total sales for the February–April 2026 period were up 4.4% from the same period a year ago, while food services and drinking places were up 2.7% from April 2025.

articles.headline: New Sales and Inventory Numbers Reflect Cautious Consumers and Retailers
articles.summary: New retail sales and wholesale inventory data show consumers growing more cautious as inflation accelerates, with the nominal retail sales increase reflecting higher prices rather than more units sold. Some wholesalers are building inventories in anticipation of further fuel cost increases, while demand for big-ticket items such as cars and furniture is softening. Supply chain management experts noted wholesalers are front-loading purchases ahead of back-to-school and holiday seasons to lock in current prices before further inflation.

articles.headline: Retail Q1 2026: Low Availability and Construction Slow Absorption
articles.summary: Q1 2026 retail market reports from CBRE, JLL, Newmark, and others showed negative net absorption across nearly all tracked reports, driven by a wave of store closures from multiple bankruptcy filings adding available space to the market. Consumer sentiment was negatively affected by lingering inflation, uncertainty about the job market, and the impact of the Iran conflict on fuel costs, per Newmark analysts, though retail sales and consumer spending remained in positive territory. Sun Belt markets outpaced the rest of the country in retail metrics driven by population growth, and JLL noted that for the remainder of 2026, performance will depend more on which markets a portfolio is in than on national averages.

articles.headline: House Cuts Build-To-Rent Ban From Latest Bill, Targets Vote Next Week
articles.summary: The House removed a ban on build-to-rent housing from its latest legislative package and is targeting a vote the following week on the modified bill, after President Trump publicly pushed House members to pass a housing bill that had included a forced-sale provision for BTR properties. The real estate lobby had sounded the alarm over the forced-sale provision in the original bill, arguing it would chill investment in single-family rental development. The modified bill's passage timeline remains uncertain pending negotiations among House members.

articles.headline: Hapag-Lloyd Q1 2026 Loss: Strait of Hormuz Chaos and Weak Freight Rates Hit Shipping
articles.summary: Hapag-Lloyd reported a Q1 2026 net loss of €219 million ($257 million), compared to a profit of €446 million in Q1 2025, as lower freight rates and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted global shipping operations. Average freight rates fell 9.5% year-over-year to $1,330 per TEU, and hundreds of commercial vessels carrying up to 20,000 seafarers remained unable to transit the Strait since the U.S. and Israel began attacks on Iran in late February 2026. Brent crude prices nearly doubled during the quarter, ending March at $118.35 per barrel, while low-sulfur bunker fuel prices surged more than 80% from year-end 2025 levels. The company maintained its full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance of $1.1 billion to $3.1 billion but warned the outlook remains subject to 'considerable uncertainty.'

articles.headline: Traders Now See Next Fed Interest Rate Move as a Hike Following Inflation Surge
articles.summary: Following a week of hotter-than-expected inflation readings, fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike as soon as December 2026, the first time in the current cycle markets have priced in a hike rather than a cut. A December hike carries a nearly 51% probability, January a 60% probability, and March better than 71%, per CME Group's FedWatch tool. The Survey of Professional Forecasters released Friday projects Q2 consumer price inflation to hit 6%, a dramatic revision from the prior 2.7% estimate, driven largely by energy prices tied to the Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz. Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, confirmed by the Senate Wednesday, inherits an increasingly complicated inflation picture as GDP growth is simultaneously revised down to 2.2% for the full year.

articles.headline: Treasury Yields Surge as Inflation Data Points to Tricky Rates Path for New Fed Chair Warsh
articles.summary: U.S. Treasury yields spiked Friday following a week of elevated inflation data, with the 10-year note surging nearly 14 basis points to 4.595% and the 30-year bond jumping to just over 5.1%, its highest level since May 2025. The 2-year yield rose close to 9 basis points to 4.079%. Import prices rose 1.9% in April and 4.2% on a 12-month basis — the largest annual gain since October 2022 — while export prices surged 8.8%, the highest since September 2022, as Middle East conflict keeps energy prices elevated. West Texas Intermediate crude rose to $104.39 per barrel, up $3.22, after the Trump-Xi summit concluded with little to show on energy diplomacy.

articles.headline: Bonds, Stocks and Precious Metals Slump as Inflation Fears Mount, Silver Falls 7%
articles.summary: Global government bonds, precious metals, and international stocks sold off Friday as inflation fears intensified and President Trump concluded a three-day visit to China with no meaningful agreement on energy or trade. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in nearly a year at 4.544%, while money markets priced in a near-zero chance of any Fed rate cuts this year and a 50% chance of a December hike, per CME FedWatch. Silver fell 7% on the session. The combination of Iran war energy shocks, ongoing tariff uncertainty, and political upheaval in the U.K. weighed on cross-asset sentiment globally.

articles.headline: Global Bond Selloff Worsens as Rising Oil Prices Spook Investors
articles.summary: Global government bond markets fell sharply on May 15, with US 10-year Treasury yields rising 12 basis points to 4.6% and 30-year yields approaching 5.12%—the highest since 2007—as Brent crude climbed past $107 per barrel amid an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff following the Iran war. The selloff was compounded by back-to-back US government reports showing consumer and wholesale prices accelerating at the fastest pace since 2022, with traders now pricing a near two-thirds probability of a Fed rate hike in December. Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, narrowly confirmed by the Senate this week, faces the selloff as his first major test. The S&P 500 fell more than 1% on Friday, pulling back from a recent rally, while gas prices nationally held above $4.50 per gallon—up 51% since the Iran war began.

articles.headline: Companies Are Getting Tariff Refunds. Here's What They Plan to Do With the Money.
articles.summary: The US Customs and Border Protection began processing the first wave of electronic tariff refunds on May 12, returning billions of dollars to importers who paid levies later struck down by the Supreme Court in February 2026. CBP said about 15% of submitted claims were rejected due to incorrect information or ineligible shipments. Major companies including General Motors said they expect hundreds of millions of dollars in refunds; Citi analysis found Walmart is owed approximately $10 billion, Target $2 billion, and Nike $1 billion. Companies have stated plans to use refunds to pay down debt, rehire workers, restock inventory, or potentially lower prices, while consumers are not directly eligible for refunds.

articles.headline: The New Route Around Hormuz Involves a Massive Convoy of Trucks
articles.summary: With the Strait of Hormuz closed following the outbreak of war in Iran, shippers and logistics operators have developed an alternative overland route using massive truck convoys to move energy and cargo around the conflict zone. The closure of the strait has driven Brent crude above $107 per barrel, up more than 10% this week alone, creating severe cost pressure across global supply chains. Trump-Xi summit talks in Beijing this week failed to produce breakthroughs on reopening the strait, with China calling for rapid reopening but no concrete agreement reached. The alternative convoy route adds significant transit time and cost compared to the standard maritime passage.

articles.headline: US Shopping Data Is Good, But Something Worrisome Is Lurking
articles.summary: Bloomberg's Retail Monitor reported that US retail sales data this week showed surface-level strength in consumer spending, but that rising oil prices above $105 per barrel and surging bond yields are creating a worrisome undercurrent for forward consumer demand. Producer price data released this week showed costs accelerating at the fastest pace since 2022, signaling potential margin compression for retailers and goods distributors. The inflation pressures stem from the combined effect of the Strait of Hormuz closure and ongoing tariff-related cost pass-through still working through supply chains. Analysts noted the combination of high gas prices—nationally averaging $4.50 per gallon—and tightening financial conditions presents a risk to the consumer spending outlook in the coming months.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules Unanimously: Freight Broker C.H. Robinson Faces Negligent Hiring Lawsuit
articles.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled unanimously this week that freight broker C.H. Robinson can face a state-law negligent hiring lawsuit from plaintiff Shawn Montgomery, rejecting the argument that federal law shields brokers from such claims. The ruling found that plaintiffs can bring state-law negligent hiring claims against freight brokers, removing a key legal protection the industry had relied upon. Industry analysts noted the ruling is expected to raise insurance premiums across the brokerage sector, tighten carrier vetting standards, and increase barriers to entry for new brokers. Over time, tighter carrier qualification standards are expected to reduce available capacity and place upward pressure on freight rates.

articles.headline: Perfectus Aluminum and Related Companies Agree to Pay $549.5M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Relating to Evaded Customs Duties
articles.summary: Perfectus Aluminum Inc. and affiliated companies agreed to pay $549.5 million to settle False Claims Act allegations that they evaded customs duties on aluminum imports, in one of the largest customs fraud settlements in US history. The case involved allegations of tariff evasion through misclassification of aluminum products to avoid anti-dumping and countervailing duties. The settlement signals intensified federal enforcement of customs compliance as part of the broader crackdown on tariff evasion following the Supreme Court's ruling on IEEPA tariffs. Importers, freight brokers, and 3PLs are expected to face heightened customs scrutiny as a result of the case.

articles.headline: Amazon Rolls Out 30-Minute Delivery on Thousands of Groceries and Essentials
articles.summary: Amazon launched a 30-minute delivery service covering thousands of grocery and everyday essentials items, expanding its ultra-fast fulfillment capabilities to a broader product set beyond its existing same-day offerings. The service relies on Amazon's network of urban micro-fulfillment nodes and delivery infrastructure. The rollout follows Amazon's May 4 launch of Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS), which opened its full logistics network to third-party businesses. The 30-minute delivery expansion intensifies pressure on traditional grocery retailers and last-mile delivery providers, and requires continued investment in dense, last-mile warehouse infrastructure.

articles.headline: project44 Launches Autopilot to Cut Freight Costs, Improve Data Quality, Optimize Inventory Levels, and Accelerate Cash Flow
articles.summary: Supply chain visibility platform project44 launched 'Autopilot,' an AI-driven tool designed to autonomously cut freight costs, improve shipment data quality, optimize inventory levels, and accelerate cash flow for shippers and logistics operators. The system uses machine learning to make automated decisions across freight procurement, routing, and inventory positioning without requiring manual intervention from supply chain teams. The launch comes as shippers face elevated freight costs due to oil price spikes from the Strait of Hormuz closure and continued tariff-related supply chain disruptions. project44 positions Autopilot as a response to the growing complexity of operating supply chains in a volatile trade and energy environment.

articles.headline: The Energy Crisis Is Becoming a Currency Crisis in Asia's Emerging Markets
articles.summary: Bloomberg Opinion reports that the Iran conflict-driven energy price shock is spreading into a currency crisis across Asian emerging markets, with major energy importers including the Philippine peso, South Korean won, Thai baht, and Egyptian pound among the worst-performing currencies since the start of the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran. The supply-side energy shock has spread into food systems, financial markets, and regional economies, raising concerns about stagflation. India has asked the U.S. to extend its waiver on Russian oil cargo sales beyond the May 16 expiry date. The disruption is affecting global shipping routes, container costs, and supply chain reliability.

articles.headline: Construction Material Costs Rose 6.2% Through April, Pressuring CRE Projects
articles.summary: Construction material costs rose 6.2% through April 2026, with energy, steel, and lumber prices climbing and pressuring commercial real estate development projects across the country. As of April 2026, steel, aluminum, and copper items carry a 50% tariff, with derivatives at 25% and industrial/electrical equipment incorporating those materials facing a 15% tariff. Associated Builders and Contractors data shows nonresidential construction input prices surged at a 12.6% annualized rate during the first two months of 2026, the fastest pace since the supply chain disruptions of early 2022. The industry needs approximately 349,000 net new workers in 2026 beyond normal hiring levels to maintain supply-demand equilibrium, with the shortage described as structural rather than cyclical.

articles.headline: Starbucks Announces Third Round of U.S. Layoffs, 300 Corporate Employees Cut
articles.summary: Starbucks announced it will lay off 300 U.S. corporate employees in its third round of job cuts as part of its ongoing turnaround strategy under CEO Brian Niccol. The coffee giant is also closing some regional support offices, with combined severance costs and office space reassessment expected to result in $400 million in restructuring charges. Starbucks expects to record $280 million in noncash charges tied to asset impairments and $120 million in cash charges related to the layoffs. This follows an earlier round that cut 1,100 jobs and another that eliminated 900 nonretail positions as part of a $1 billion restructuring plan.

articles.headline: Xi and Trump Map Out a New Framework
articles.summary: President Trump concluded his visit to Beijing with Xi Jinping, announcing deals and a new strategic framework for the US-China economic relationship. The summit addressed a range of economic and geopolitical issues including trade tensions, tariff levels, semiconductors, and AI. The current US-China trade status quo is set to expire in November, creating urgency around the talks. Analysts noted that while the optics were positive, major sticking points remained unresolved.

articles.headline: ITS Logistics May Port/Rail Ramp Freight Index: Strait of Hormuz Closure Sends Fuel Shock Through Supply Chains
articles.summary: ITS Logistics released its May Port/Rail Ramp Freight Index reporting elevated status across Atlantic and Gulf port regions, with container termination challenges at key West Coast gateways. The ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz is pushing fuel costs higher, with retail diesel reaching $5.639 per gallon as of May 11—a jump of nearly 29 cents since the end of April. FTR Transportation Intelligence reported spot market rates approached all-time highs during the week of May 8, driven by fuel cost pass-through and tightening capacity. The Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance's annual International Roadcheck began May 12, with an out-of-service rate of 31.4% further tightening trucking capacity.
